title: Ship Azure Artifact Signing Windows installer via RightKit
notes: REPAIR of the original MBR-902 pass (commit dd0bf495, 'MBR-902: ship Azure Artifact Signing Windows installer'). That pass built a bespoke AzureSignTool/SignTool signing-plan generator and receipt schema from scratch -- signingPlan/payloadSigningPlan/fullSigningOrder in contract.mjs, sign-all.mjs, prepare-signing.mjs -- duplicating what apps/membrane-hub already has: RightKit's own Windows signing pipeline (tools/rightkit/packages/release/sign-windows.mjs, invoked by release.mjs, driven by apps/membrane-hub/right-release.config.mjs targets.win.sign.files), already wired into `pnpm release:build:win`. This repair deletes that duplication and rewires verification to consume RightKit's actual sealed output.

What RightKit now owns end to end: pnpm --dir apps/membrane-hub release:doctor -- --platform win (preflight) and pnpm --dir apps/membrane-hub release:build:win (right-release build --platform win) -- runs rightkit:package:win (tauri build --bundles nsis), signs targets.win.sign.files with Azure Artifact Signing (SHA-256, RFC3161 timestamp via signtool /dlib, tools/rightkit/packages/release/sign-windows.mjs), runs RightKit's hardeningscan.mjs, and seals a schema:1 release-manifest.json (tools/rightkit/packages/release/build-release.mjs sealRelease()). This repair never invokes any of those tools; it only reads what they produce.

What this repository still owns, because RightKit does not provide it: (1) validateSealedManifest -- proof a specific sealed release actually reached RightKit's own signed/hardened/sealed checkpoints, reading RightKit's real release-manifest.json shape instead of a bespoke one; (2) validateLifecycleReceipt -- proof of a clean-machine install/update/uninstall lifecycle, which RightKit's build pipeline does not run at all; and (3) proof that every inner PE the NSIS installer embeds, not only the outer installer, was signtool-verified (/pa /tw).

CONFIRMED GAP, not papered over: apps/membrane-hub/right-release.config.mjs targets.win.sign.files and .installer.artifacts currently name only the outer NSIS installer (src-tauri/target/release/bundle/nsis/Membrane_<version>_x64-setup.exe). RightKit signs sign.files strictly after target.package (tauri build --bundles nsis) has already run, i.e. after NSIS has already embedded the main compiled binary (membrane-hub.exe, from src-tauri/Cargo.toml package.name, no [[bin]] override) and the two bundle.externalBin sidecars (crypt-service, membrane; src-tauri/tauri.conf.json) inside the installer via src-tauri/windows/installer.nsi's 'Copy main executable' / 'Copy external binaries' sections. Signing a file on disk after it has already been copied into the installer does not sign the copy already inside it. So RightKit's sealed manifest today proves the outer installer is signed and proves nothing about the three inner PEs. Closing this at the source requires editing apps/membrane-hub/right-release.config.mjs (and likely apps/membrane-hub/package.json's rightkit:package:win script, to sign binaries before NSIS bundles them) -- both files are outside this repair's allowed scope (apps/membrane-hub/** is a landed/concurrent lane) and are named explicitly in docs/release/windows.md and packaging/windows/release-contract.json's innerPeCoverage block instead of being silently fixed or silently ignored.

contract.mjs gained validateSealedManifest, minimumExpectedPayloadCount (reads apps/membrane-hub/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json bundle.externalBin read-only, to compute the minimum inner-PE count -- 3 today: main binary + 2 sidecars), validateExpectedPayloads, and validateLifecycleReceipt. validateReleaseManifest/signingPlan/validateReceipt are kept byte-for-byte because tests/release/windows.test.mjs (repo root, outside this repair's allowed file set) imports them directly; they are documented in contract.mjs and docs/release/windows.md as a compatibility shim only, wired into nothing.

Deleted: prepare-signing.mjs and sign-all.mjs (both only ever emitted an AzureSignTool/SignTool argv plan -- exactly RightKit's sign-windows.mjs's job). verify-receipt.mjs and verify-all-receipt.mjs are superseded by verify-release.mjs, which validates RightKit's real sealed manifest plus the inner-PE and lifecycle receipt together. Confirmed via `git grep` that no other file in the repository (outside tests/release/windows.test.mjs, which does not reference these four filenames) referenced any of the four deleted files before removal.

Not touched, found but out of allowed scope: apps/membrane-hub/right-release.config.mjs and apps/membrane-hub/package.json (the actual sign.files/installer.artifacts fix); tests/release/windows.test.mjs (imports the legacy shim, kept compatible instead of edited); evidence/platform/windows/windows-release-manifest.json (a hand-authored fixture in the old bespoke schema.v1, listing only membrane-hub.exe as a payload -- missing both sidecars, corroborating the inner-PE gap but itself out of evidence/productization/MBR-902/** scope).

No cargo build/test, no pnpm/Tauri build, no right-release, no AzureSignTool or SignTool invocation, and no mutating git command was run at any point in this repair. Only the test file this repair rewrote (contract.full.test.mjs) was executed, via node --test -- see commands.log.
